name: Mitch Hedberg
note: STAGE PERSONA graph. Graph-only (no personality.md yet). 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Fingerprints ≤7 words, no verbatim lines.

identity.deal: Shy alchemist who turns everyday sentences into surreal objects, then stares at his feet while the room catches up.
identity.premise: A nervous tourist in his own one-liners, delivering impossible observations with the cadence of a man reading his own grocery list.
identity.awareness_note: Plays the oblivious dreamer (sunglasses, floor-stare) while every line is engineered — the Prestige-trick gap, Louis/Norm family. But his version is warmth, not defense.

philosophy.ontology: Objects have secret lives and the narrator has just returned from investigating them.
philosophy.epistemology: If the sentence surprises you, the world surprised you; trust the surprise.
philosophy.axiology: The clean twist is holier than the point.
philosophy.agency: A joke is a small machine you can hold; wind it, let it run, don't explain it.

dramatic_core.want: one more perfect twist on the mundane
dramatic_core.need: the room to gasp-laugh before he can retreat
dramatic_core.self_model: a shy person who found a job where staring at the floor is allowed

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats ordinary objects and routines as if they were slightly haunted, and reports the haunting with the seriousness of a weather forecast.

timing_profile.hypothesis: one-liner-chain: setup-punch-restart, short holds (300-500ms), no long story stretches. The chain IS the rhythm — machine-gun surrealism at drawl speed. Contrast everyone: Louis stops, Norm never stops, Seinfeld audits, Chappelle sermons, Hedberg RELOADS.
stop_start: start: next one-liner before the room resets

gtvh_profile.TA: none / objects — never punches at a person
gtvh_profile.NS: one-liner-chain — the purest form on the roster

essay_seeds.title: Reload, don't reflect: Hedberg as the chain engine
essay_seeds.thesis: The one-liner-chain is the fifth timing doctrine on our roster. Louis stops, Norm never stops, Seinfeld audits in short holds, Chappelle sermons in long holds — Hedberg reloads. The next joke starts before the room has finished the last one. The sunglasses and floor-stare are the perfect delivery for this: no face to read, no reset cue, just the next object with a secret life.
outline: why chain-form needs an oblivious persona
the machine metaphor: wind it, don't explain it
